spot.html_text: In Väänänen’s logics it is easy to see why one needs sets of assignments, i.e. teams. He has an atomic formula, called a dependence atom , expressing ‘ ⟦M⟧ is dependent on ⟦M⟧ ’, or more exactly, ‘ ⟦M⟧ is totally determined by ⟦M⟧ ’. How can we interpret this in a structure, for example the structure of natural numbers? It makes no sense at all to ask for example whether 8 is dependent on 37. spot.html_text: There are two players. In general we can call them ⟦M⟧ and ⟦M⟧ . The pronunciations ‘Abelard’ and ‘Eloise’ go back to the mid 1980s and usefully fix the players as male and female making reference easier: her move, his move. Other names are in common use for the players in particular types of logical game.
